forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Teignbridge cuts forecast funding gaps by nearly half as audit work to regain assurance accelerates
news_drafts.lead: Teignbridge District Council faces a disclaimed audit opinion, the lowest form of external audit assurance, for 2025/26 and has held this status since 2020/21. However, the council's financial position is improving. Forecast funding gaps for 2027/28 and 2028/29 have fallen from £3.6 million and £2.8 million to £1.13 million and £0.95 million, driven partly by drawing only £680,000 from reserves in 2025/26 against a budgeted £1.5 million. The Ministry of Housing and Communities and Local Government upgraded Teignbridge's audit assessment ranking from D to C. Regaining assurance work, originally scheduled for 2030–31, is now prioritised to begin in 2027, backed by £42,388 in government grant funding. Internal audits have identified control gaps: licensing income lacks regular reconciliation; the self-build register requires cleansing; and car park audit recommendations from February 2024 remain largely unimplemented, with only two of ten completed. Financial resilience has been marked as a critical audit priority.

findings.paper_title: Q1 Audit Scrutiny 29.09.26 - Strategic & Corporate Risk Report
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creating new emerging risks as Devon councils explore merger
findings.detail: New risks are emerging at Pan Devon and Teignbridge level as councils progress towards local government reorganisation. A separate LGR-specific risk register has been drafted. Officer workshop scheduled 28 September 2026 to review and ensure risks are properly owned with clear mitigation KPIs.
findings.matters: LGR creates significant uncertainty around council's future financial position, operational capacity, and service delivery; represents emerging risk landscape requiring active management
findings.figures: Officer workshop scheduled 28 September 2026; Q2 engagement phase ongoing
findings.quote: New risks are emerging at both a Pan Devon and Teignbridge level as the journey towards local government reorganisation in Devon progresses, and a separate risk register has been drafted to capture those affecting Teignbridge.

findings.paper_title: Q1 Audit Scrutiny 29.09.26 - Strategic & Corporate Risk Report
findings.headline: Structural financial risks persist despite controls and remain sensitive to external economic pressures
findings.detail: Three strategic financial risks continue: economic uncertainty (ST08, score 9 medium), failure to control/manage finance (ST02, score 8 medium), and income collection failure (CP07, score 4 low). All are managed through budget monitoring and 3-year planning, but the paper explicitly states these structural risks remain sensitive to external economic shocks.
findings.matters: Council's financial position remains exposed to economic downturn and income volatility; mitigation effectiveness depends on economic conditions staying stable
findings.figures: ST08 score: 9 (medium); ST02 score: 8 (medium); CP07 score: 4 (low)
findings.quote: Financial risks are managed but remain sensitive to external pressures. While no immediate financial crisis is identified, several structural financial risks remain

findings.paper_title: Q1 Audit Scrutiny 29.09.26 - Strategic & Corporate Risk Report
findings.headline: Comprehensive Risk Management Strategy review initiated following internal audit findings
findings.detail: A March 2026 Devon Assurance Partnership risk workshop and recommendations from an internal audit review of risk management arrangements have triggered a complete review of the council's Risk Management Strategy. Engagement with risk owners scheduled for Q2-Q3 2026, with formal approval expected afterwards.
findings.matters: Audit recommendations indicate prior gaps in risk management were identified; strengthened governance frameworks reduce unidentified risk emerging
findings.figures: Strategy review commenced; officer workshop 28 September 2026
findings.quote: The outcomes of this workshop, together with recommendations arising from the recent internal audit review of risk management arrangements, have triggered a comprehensive review of the Council's Risk Management Strategy.

findings.paper_title: Q1 Audit Scrutiny 29.09.26 - Strategic & Corporate Risk Report
findings.headline: Health & Safety and Cyber Security remain the council's highest-scoring residual risks despite mitigation efforts
findings.detail: Two risks carry mitigated scores of 12 (high): ST11 (Failure to comply with H&S legislation) and ST46 (Failure of ICT security measures). Both have unmitigated scores of 20 (very high). Despite multiple ongoing mitigation actions and governance improvements, neither risk has improved its mitigated score, indicating these vulnerabilities persist.
findings.matters: H&S failures expose council to prosecution, corporate manslaughter liability, and reputational damage; cyber attacks could cause service disruption, data corruption, and financial loss
findings.figures: ST11: mitigated score 12 (unmitigated 20); ST46: mitigated score 12 (unmitigated 20)
findings.quote: While Health & Safety and Cyber Security remain the council's principal residual risks, there is evidence of increasingly mature governance, stronger challenge, and greater transparency in risk reporting.

findings.paper_title: Q1 Audit Scrutiny 29.09.26 - Strategic & Corporate Risk Report
findings.headline: General Balances increased by £2.6m, boosting financial resilience
findings.detail: General Balances have been increased by approximately £2.6m, listed as a key control mechanism for managing strategic financial risks. This strengthens the council's financial buffer against external economic shocks and unexpected pressures.
findings.matters: Directly improves council's capacity to absorb financial volatility and economic downturns without operational impact
